name: monday.com
summary: Work management platform with boards, automations and views — plus separately-priced CRM, Dev and Service products.
best_for: teams who want one visual system for projects and work, and who will actually use the automations and views that justify the per-seat price at Standard or above
skip_if: you are two or three people who need a shared list. The free tier caps at 2 seats and 3 boards, and paying per seat for views you will not use is the most common way this gets expensive. Also skip it if you only want the CRM, since that is a separate subscription and worth pricing against dedicated CRMs
honest_knock: The seat price is not the product price. monday sells four products — Work Management, CRM, Dev and Service — each on its own subscription, and the $9 you see first is the cheapest tier of one of them. A sales team that wants the CRM is buying a second subscription on top of whatever Work Management costs, with a three-seat minimum of its own. The second number to find before you commit is the automation cap. Standard allows 250 automation actions a month across the whole account. If you are buying monday because of the automations you saw demoed, 250 is roughly one workflow running a few times a day — and the next step up is Pro at $19 a seat against Standard's $12. Free is capped at two seats and three boards, which makes it a preview rather than a plan. On payment, the FAQ excludes debit cards (credit card or PayPal, depending on location) and accepts invoices only for Enterprise orders above a minimum fee it does not state, which can rule monday out for a small company that pays by bank transfer.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-08-26 on monday.com/pricing over a US connection, at their default of 10 seats on yearly billing; re-read 2026-09-29 in a rendered browser from a Dutch connection, where the page serves euros with the same numerals on all three paid tiers and the AI-credit line with its equal 'special monthly discount' is unchanged; re-read 2026-10-21 from a Dutch connection, same euro numerals, the same 18% yearly saving and the same AI-credit lines; re-read 2026-10-23 with a plain fetch, again unchanged) Free covers two seats. Basic is $9 per seat a month, a total of $90; Standard $12, down from $14, for $120 instead of $140; Pro $19, down from $22, for $190 instead of $220. Enterprise is quoted. The seat count is the thing to watch: the per-seat figure moves with team size, so a price read at ten seats is not what three or fifty will cost. Yearly billing is marked as 18% off, and each paid tier carries its own monthly AI-credit allowance rather than selling AI separately.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 28 October 2026 on the free Pro trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We imported three made-up tasks, set up one automation, asked the AI assistant one question, exported the board, imported it again with one change and opened the Pro checkout without entering a card.
findings: The account opened on a 14-day Pro trial without a card, after six onboarding screens. The first screen had 'allow automatic sign-ups with an @aibuildermarketplace.com email address' switched on by default.

The plans page started at 5 seats; the smallest choice was 3. For 3 seats Pro cost €19 per seat a month billed yearly or €24 monthly, and choosing monthly first opened a prompt to reconsider yearly billing.

The Pro checkout for 3 seats monthly added an AI add-on of €30 (3,000 credits) by itself, offset by a €30 discount 'only in the first year', plus €15.12 tax (21%): €87.12 a month. After the first year that add-on would cost extra if you keep it.

Our CSV import matched only the Status column automatically; task name and due date had to be mapped by hand. Start Date arrived as a text column. The status cells first showed colours without labels, but the labels appeared after reloading the board.

A 'when status changes to Done, move item to group' automation ran within seconds and used 1 of the 25,000 monthly actions on Pro. The Sidekick assistant correctly named the two tasks due on 29 October.
Re-importing with one changed description and 'Update' matched on task name: the description changed and no duplicates appeared, although the notice said '3 items imported'.

Invitations offer Admin, Member and a Viewer role described as 'view only, no edits (free)'. The 'downgrade to Free' link only said you can choose a plan when the trial ends. API tokens and an MCP server are offered in the developer centre.
not_tested: What the Free plan allows after the trial
How many AI credits one Sidekick answer uses (we saw a balance of 7.6 afterwards, not before)
Guests and seat costs with real colleagues
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

vendor_mcp.what: Hosted server covering boards, items, updates and workspace data, discoverable through a machine-readable card at monday.com/.well-known/mcp.json.
vendor_mcp.plan: Their own FAQ, in two sentences: "MCP is currently available for all monday.com plans" and "There is currently no additional cost to use monday MCP." They add the caveat most vendors leave out — you may still pay the AI client you run it from.
vendor_mcp.note: The vendor's own MCP server, from our MCP research; it works with your own account at the vendor.

agent_checkout.detail: No explicit support for purchases by AI agents on the vendor's own pages.
